Hi Anya — quick technical notes to supplement Lauren’s attachments. I’m quoting a couple of your RFI asks below for context.

> Tab: Data Classification — Describe how PII is categorized and where it persists

- Classification: Redwood classifies incoming customer content into three buckets: Sensitive PII (names, unredacted SSNs, payment data), Identifiers (emails, device IDs), and Non-PII. We annotate tokens for processing but do not persist full-customer text in long-term logs unless explicit logging is enabled by the customer.

- Persistence: Customer content is processed in-memory on inference nodes. We persist model audit logs (request metadata, token counts, error traces) and optional application logs. If a customer opts into long-term request storage for analytics, content storage is enabled and encrypted. Default: short-term ephemeral buffers only.

> Tab: KMS Key Custody

- Key model: Hosted API customers can use Redwood-managed KMS keys (Google/AWS KMS) or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via Cloud KMS/HSM integration. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-provided KMS with local HSM available.
- Attestation: Attached kms_attestation_summary.pdf — lists key usage policies, rotation windows, and separation of duties. If MedicaTech requires a deeper attestation (letter or signed artifact), let us know and we can coordinate with Security.

> Tab: Subprocessors / Cross-border

- Subprocessors: attached CSV includes countries and processing purposes. We limit subprocessors that handle content tokens; many infra services are US/EU based.
- Transfers: Redwood supports region pinning for data residency (US/EU/APAC). When region pinning is not used, we rely on contractual SCCs + standard contractual clauses for cross-border processing.

If you want a short, one-line description for each subprocessor (for procurement sheet), I can produce that by EOD tomorrow.

—
